mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which increases corporate costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE < 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening economy, boosting consumer confidence and increasing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in > 40% of instances where HOUST increases over three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above a 3-month moving average signals increased economic activity, which positively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in > 50% of instances where INDPRO > 3-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) coupled with a decrease in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals a monetary policy intended to stimulate demand, which positively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances where both FEDFUNDS and RSAFS decrease.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and increases S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a strong economic growth, which positively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in > 40% of instances where GDPC1 increases over two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% signals an aggressive easing cycle, which boosts equity markets and increases S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 1%.
